exposure: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) undergoing scoliosis surgery
Lowest instrumented vertebra (L3, L4, above L3, above L4)
outcome: Type of analgesia for Cesarean section
cohort: The study included 205 women with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis who underwent spinal fusion surgery and 173 healthy women, with both groups further divided into pregnant and non-pregnant cohorts.
finding: Women with a history of spinal fusion for AIS, particularly those fused to L3 or L4, reported a higher incidence of low back pain during pregnancy and more frequently required Cesarean sections, but showed general satisfaction with their health-related quality of life similar to healthy controls.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed more frequently in women with scoliosis surgery and pregnancy (64%) compared to healthy pregnant controls (33%), with this risk increasing to 55% when spinal fusion to L4 was performed, and general anesthesia was more often required for those fused to L4.
